pulserver#

The root namespace is the plugin contract: the base class a sequence plugin subclasses, the abstract types it exchanges with the authoring namespace, the typed parameters its scanner UI is built from, and the offline CLI.

It deliberately exports no authoring helpers. Those are split across two namespaces by role, so a plugin’s parts stay visibly separate:

import pulserver.pypulseq as pp           # events, Sequence, Opts
import pulserver.design as design         # modules and scan loops
from pulserver import Sequence, UIParam   # plugin contract

pulserver.pypulseq is the event layer: upstream PyPulseq re-exported whole, plus Pulserver’s replacements for a few of its objects. pulserver.design is the toolbox above it — every factory returning a SequenceModule or a ScanLoop.

Ready-to-run sequence callbacks are intentionally a separate public namespace: pulserver.sequences. They accept explicit sequence controls and return a pulserver.pypulseq.Sequence, while this root namespace continues to hold the bridge/plugin contract.

Plugin contracts#

The base class a plugin builds on, plus the entry point that turns one into a command-line tool. Sequence (alias PulseqSequence) declares the default protocol and synthesises the .seq file.

pulserver.PulseqSequence

Base class that every pulserver sequence plugin must satisfy.

pulserver.Sequence

pulserver.run_cli

Run a plugin's offline CLI from a declarative flag→protocol mapping.

Abstract types#

The things every pulserver.design factory returns, named here because they are part of the contract rather than of any one waveform family. There are two, plus the descriptor that annotates one of them:

Type

Question

Feeds

SequenceModule

what do I play?

seq.add_block(*block)

ScanLoop

what varies, in what order?

lin_idx/par_idx, rotation, freq_offset_hz

EncodingAxis

what does one column of that loop mean?

the counter it emits, the converter that applies

There is one loop type, not one per axis. A ScanLoop is a table of positions, a grouping of them into shots — one shot being one excitation’s worth of the loop — and one EncodingAxis per position column. An encoding position is a set of frequency offsets, gradient scalings and rotations, and nothing about that restricts it to k-space: a Cartesian echo train, a non-Cartesian view list, an SMS slice group, a dynamic frame and an inversion-time series are the same table under different axis declarations. The axis fixes which converter applies (to_scales, to_rotations, to_frequencies) and which counter labels() emits.

A module answers to four independent setters: set_state (the numbers that re-render its waveforms), set_labels (per-shot counters), set_flags (sticky block properties, scoped to the module) and set_triggers (trigger and digital-output events, per block).

Neither type owns the loop itself. How frames, slices, contrasts and shots nest is plain for statements in the plugin, which is what keeps a preparation, a trigger or a dummy TR insertable at any level.

pulserver.ScanLoop

One ordered list of scan-loop iterations: what varies, and in what order.

pulserver.SequenceModule

A reusable group of Pulseq blocks that re-renders itself per shot.

pulserver.EncodingAxis

One named dimension of a ScanLoop.

Protocol parameter types#

One class per scanner UI control. Each carries the value, its display unit, and the bounds the interpreter enforces, so a single object drives both the UI and the offline default protocol.

pulserver.BoolParam

Boolean toggle parameter.

pulserver.Description

Read-only text row: a section header or an explanatory note.

pulserver.DropdownFloatParam

Float parameter offering preset values plus free type-in.

pulserver.DropdownIntParam

Integer parameter offering preset values plus free type-in.

pulserver.StringListParam

String-list parameter with an explicit selected value.

pulserver.TypeinFloatParam

Float parameter displayed as a GE type-in control.

pulserver.TypeinIntParam

Integer parameter displayed as a GE type-in control.

Protocol keys and enumerations#

UIParam is the canonical key namespace every protocol is written against. The *Key groups record which value type each key expects; the remaining enumerations are the fixed option sets behind dropdown controls.

pulserver.BoolKey

Canonical keys whose values must be boolean parameters.

pulserver.EnumKey

Canonical keys whose values must be string-list (enum) parameters.

pulserver.FloatKey

Canonical keys whose values must be float parameters.

pulserver.ImagingMode

Acquisition dimensionality shown in the UI.

pulserver.InputMode

How a numeric parameter is presented in the GE interpreter UI.

pulserver.IntKey

Canonical keys whose values must be integer parameters.

pulserver.ParamKind

Value kind a canonical protocol key expects.

pulserver.PreparationType

Preparation pulse family shown in the UI.

pulserver.SequenceType

Pulse sequence family shown in the UI.

pulserver.TriggerType

Trigger source selection shown in the UI.

pulserver.UIParam

Convenience namespace exposing all canonical protocol keys.

pulserver.Validate

Validation strategy applied to a protocol parameter.

Protocol and ProtocolValue are the mapping and value type aliases used by the helpers below.

Protocol handling#

The four calls a plugin actually makes: validate a protocol, round-trip it between typed parameter objects and the plain-dictionary form exchanged with the interpreter, and build a dropdown from an enumeration. The per-entry and per-parameter primitives underneath them are implementation detail and stay in pulserver._core.

pulserver.dict_to_protocol

Deserialize nested plain dictionaries back into a typed protocol.

pulserver.make_enum_param

Create a StringListParam for an enum-backed control.

pulserver.protocol_to_dict

Serialize a whole protocol to nested plain dictionaries.

pulserver.validate_protocol

Check every entry of a protocol against its key's declared type.

Protocol accessors#

pulserver.params reads and writes protocol values by canonical key and resolves derived quantities — phase FOV, ACS size, readout/phase axes — that plugins would otherwise each recompute.

pulserver.params

Read and write protocol values, and resolve the quantities derived from them.
